questions.q: An alkene C₅H₁₀ on ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O) gives acetone and acetaldehyde. The alkene is:
questions.explain: Facing the two C=O carbons and joining them with a double bond gives (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃. 2-Methylbut-1-ene would give butan-2-one and HCHO instead.

questions.q: 2-Methylbut-2-ene is treated with O₃ followed by H₂O₂ (oxidative work-up). The products are:
questions.explain: In an oxidative work-up each –CHO fragment becomes –COOH, but a ketone fragment stays a ketone. So the =CH–CH₃ end gives acetic acid and the (CH₃)₂C= end gives acetone.

questions.q: Benzene is treated with O₃ and then Zn/H₂O. The product is:
questions.explain: Benzene reacts as if it had three Kekulé C=C bonds, giving 3 OHC–CHO. The dialdehyde glyoxal is often confused with glycol, which ozonolysis with Zn/H₂O never gives.

questions.q: Toluene is subjected to complete ozonolysis followed by Zn/H₂O. The products are:
questions.explain: Cutting the three ring C=C bonds leaves the methyl-bearing carbon in one CH₃–CO–CHO fragment and the other four ring carbons as two OHC–CHO. Biacetyl needs two adjacent methyl-bearing carbons, as in o-xylene.
